entry_state: Versioned award terms distinguish surviving rights from delivery. The financing methods distinguish contractual cash, carrying value, classification and legal discharge. Early repurchase allocates debt and equity consideration; induced conversion measures added rights at amendment. The separate-date example releases debt on binding acceptance on 5 January and delivers shares on 20 January; its explanation continues next.
exit_state: Amendment and debt discharge have separate legal conditions. Cumulative hedge measurements determine reserve changes, with basis adjustment distinguished from recycling and cash settlement. Fair-value hedges and benchmark changes retain their own rules. The excluded-component section now introduces option time value as protection cost; its event and valuation requirements continue next.
findings: The delayed-delivery example preserves amendment-date loss and distinguishes equity recognition from the IAS 33 denominator question.
The lower-of hedge calculation is explicitly cumulative and conditional on the admitted offsetting case. Its two-period example exposes the error from applying the minimum to period increments.
The inventory example reconciles equity with a direct basis transfer; matching closing cash alone would not validate intermediate reserves.
Benchmark reform requires economic equivalence and does not reset existing reserves. No new confirmed local defect.
